title: Thermal behavior in FeCuCrCoNi high entropy alloy nanoparticles: an atomistic approach.

recollection.intervention: Large-scale atomistic (molecular-dynamics) heating/cooling simulations to follow structural evolution with temperature (guess)
recollection.structure: Initially random bcc/fcc solid-solution nanoparticles that begin to segregate Cu to the surface and develop core–shell or multiphase regions upon heating (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Element-specific melting/segregation driven by different cohesive energies; surface segregation lowers total free energy while Cr–Fe–Co–Ni remain in a mixed core (guess)
recollection.results: Predicted onset of surface premelting at ~950 K, full melting around 1350 K for 10 nm particles; Cu surface enrichment reached >60 at.% above 800 K; calculated diffusion coefficients showed Arrhenius activation energies of 0.4–0.6 eV (all approximate, guess)

score.note: Correctly identifies molecular-dynamics heating simulations, which is more specific than the title, though cooling was not part of the reported protocol. The proposed Cu surface segregation/core–shell structure and cohesive-energy segregation mechanism contradict the paper’s finding of no persistent clustering, precipitation, or substantial liquid shell. The numerical melting temperatures, Cu enrichment, particle size, and activation energies are unsupported or incorrect.
